# Two Changes to Selective Availability

Selective Availability was a feature that deliberately degraded public GPS signals for national security. It was addressed in two separate steps.

In May 2000, at President Bill Clinton’s direction, the US government stopped using the feature to make civil and commercial GPS more useful worldwide. That was the operational change.

In September 2007, the government announced that the future GPS III generation would be procured without Selective Availability. This was a separate step: not the switch in 2000, but the omission of the feature from a future generation, making the 2000 policy durable for GPS III.
